name: InteriorAI
tagline: Upload a photo of a room and get AI redesigns of it in different interior styles.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Under the hood this is image-to-image diffusion with structure conditioning: keep the room geometry, repaint the furniture and finishes, driven by a style prompt. An agent can wire that up in an afternoon with a hosted model endpoint or a local SDXL plus ControlNet depth setup, and the first outputs will look genuinely impressive. What takes longer is everything that makes the outputs usable: per-style prompt libraries that do not melt windows, masks that keep the floor plan intact, resolution and upscaling, and a queue that does not make you stare at a spinner. You also need a GPU or an API key, so this is not a pure local freebie. Buildable, worth building if you redesign rooms occasionally, not worth building if you need consistent client-ready renders.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you drop in a room photo, pick a style and room type, and get four depth-conditioned img2img redesigns saved to disk.
requirements: An image model: a Replicate API token, or a local GPU with roughly 12GB VRAM for SDXL plus a depth ControlNet
Disk space for model weights if running locally
Patience for prompt tuning per style
whatYouLose: A tuned prompt and parameter set per style that mostly avoids warped windows, floating chairs and doors to nowhere
Fast generation because someone else is paying for warm GPUs
Room type detection, masking and virtual staging modes that empty a room before refurnishing it
Mobile-friendly capture and sharing, which matters because you are photographing rooms with a phone
Higher resolution outputs and upscaling without extra plumbing
moatNotes: The technique is public. The value is knowing which sampler, strength and negative prompt combination stops the model from inventing a fifth wall.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the difference between a demo and a deliverable here is entirely in the tuning, and tuning is boring. Realtors, stagers and people mid-renovation want twenty plausible options in two minutes on a phone, not a Python environment with a broken CUDA install. There is also the honest fact that hosted GPU time at scale is cheaper per image than your own idle hardware, and if you only redesign a room twice a year, a subscription for one month costs less than a weekend of your life.
notes: The clone is easy, the render quality is not. Expect your first fifty outputs to have surrealist window placement.
prompt:
Build a local web app called RoomRedo that redesigns interior photos using image-to-image diffusion with depth conditioning.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI backend, Uvicorn.
- Plain server-rendered HTML with Jinja2 templates and a little vanilla JS. No React, no build step.
- SQLite via sqlite3 for a job history table. No ORM.
- Model calls go through Replicate's HTTP API using an SDXL or Flux image-to-image model with a depth or canny ControlNet. Read REPLICATE_API_TOKEN from .env via python-dotenv. Put the model slug in a single MODEL constant at the top of one file so it is trivial to swap.

Features in scope:
- Upload form: one room photo (jpg/png), a room type dropdown (living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, home office, dining room), a style dropdown (Scandinavian, mid-century modern, industrial, japandi, maximalist, coastal, brutalist), a strength slider 0.2 to 0.8, and a count of 1 to 4 variations.
- A styles.py module holding one dict: each style maps to a positive prompt fragment, a negative prompt fragment, and default guidance and strength. This file is the whole product, treat it as such and leave comments explaining what to tweak.
- Compose the final prompt as: style fragment + room type + "interior photograph, realistic lighting, architectural photography". Shared negative prompt covers warped geometry, extra doors, text, watermarks, distorted windows.
- Submit jobs to a background task, poll status from the browser every 2 seconds, show a spinner then the results grid.
- Save originals and outputs under ./data/images/, record every job with its full prompt and parameters in SQLite so you can see which settings produced which image.
- A /history page: side by side original and outputs, with the exact parameters printed underneath. Copy-parameters button.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, payments, sharing links, furniture shopping links, upscaling, inpainting masks, telemetry, Docker.

Deliverables: requirements.txt, .env.example with REPLICATE_API_TOKEN, a README with setup in five commands, and a note in the README stating that output quality lives or dies in styles.py and that strength above 0.6 will start rearranging the walls.
